text.title: Problem Validation 2026 Core Rules
text.summary: 9 testable rules every Problem Validation 2026 application must enforce, plus a skip-this-methodology fallback. These are HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override them.

rule.statement: Every evidence item MUST be ranked on the 5-level hierarchy (paid > committed > engaged > interested > stated); un-ranked items rejected.

rationale.source: Sean Ellis / Rob Fitzpatrick — Mom Test

rule.rationale: Behavioral commitments are costly signals; stated preferences are cheap.

rule.statement: Verdict 'validated' MUST require ≥3 tier-1 or tier-2 signals from cold (non-network) respondents.
rule.rationale: Warm contacts compliment to preserve relationship; cold strangers give unbiased signal.

rule.statement: Future-tense statements ("I would introduce you") MUST be classified as tier-4, never tier-2.

Validation MUST be re-run every 90 days and stale validations expire; in addition, every artefact MUST schedule its own next iteration (target date, target respondent count, target tier upgrade). One-shot validations are rejected.
rule.rationale: AI-adjacent markets shift faster than annual validation can catch. 90 days is the outer bound at which a validation is void, not the working cadence — an artefact that emits a verdict and is then filed with no next iteration decays within days of being written.

rule.statement: Evidence ledger MUST be authored and human-reviewed BEFORE the verdict is drafted in a separate pass.
rule.rationale: One-pass ledger+verdict anchors verdict on first evidence processed.

rule.statement: Every interview MUST open with the 5-step sequence (Vision-state → Framing-honesty → Weakness-admit → Pedestal-knock → Ask for help), and the artefact MUST carry an opener-applied flag per interview. Skipping or reordering the steps is rejected.

rationale.source: Rob Fitzpatrick — Mom Test; internal interview audits 2026

rule.rationale: The opener drops the interviewee's performance pressure. A reordered opener leaves the pedestal intact, and the answers stay flattering — which is precisely the bias r2 and r3 exist to keep out of the ledger. See templates/opener-sequence.txt.

rule.statement: Every evidence item MUST carry a commitment-signal type — Time | Reputation | Money — in addition to its hierarchy tier. Untagged evidence is rejected.
rule.rationale: The tier says how strong the signal is; the type says what behaviour produced it. Mapping tier to signal type is what makes the hierarchy operational — the interviewer knows what to watch for instead of grading a transcript after the fact. See templates/commitment-classifier.txt.

rule.statement: For every Mom-Test-failing question the team has used, a replacement past-behaviour question MUST be recorded in a per-engagement replacement table. Untracked rewrites are rejected.
rule.rationale: Without a replacement table the same bad question reappears sprint after sprint; the table is the only institutional memory of what was already learned about the script.

rule.statement: Each iteration MUST name a single accountable owner. "The team" is rejected; ownership rotates only when handed off in writing in the artefact.
rule.rationale: A recurring validation cadence dies without a named owner, and an unowned ledger is nobody's to freeze under r5.

rule.statement: If any Applies-If precondition fails OR any Skip-If condition triggers, do NOT apply this methodology. Emit a skip-record naming the failed precondition / triggered skip, and route the task to the correct methodology (or none).
rule.rationale: Mis-application produces worse artefacts than no methodology, because downstream consumers trust the schema; the skip-record makes non-application traceable.
